---
title: "Fibermorph: Automated Hair Cross-Section Morphology"
subtitle: "SAM2-guided segmentation · Elliptic Fourier Descriptors · 82-feature morphospace"
---

## Overview

Fibermorph is a fully automated pipeline for measuring the shape of hair fiber cross-sections from microscopy images. This site documents the analysis and results for a dataset of **1,737 retained masks** produced from a collection of scalp-location paired images (Region A and Region B per individual).

### Key results

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total images (valid transfer) | 1,741 |
| Masks retained | 1,737 (99.8%) |
| Shape classes | 7 (rule-based taxonomy) |
| PC1 variance explained | ~43–46% |
| Mirror compression ratio | 0.437 (2.3× closer than random) |
| Outliers (Mahalanobis > mean+3SD) | 29 / 1,737 (1.7%) |

### Pipeline summary

1. **SAM2 guided segmentation** — few-shot prototype built from manually verified reference pairs; cosine-similarity map drives point prompts; best candidate selected by composite score (see [Methods](methods.qmd)).
2. **Shape feature extraction** — 82 features per mask: geometric (8), radial profile (7), Hu moments (7), EFD coefficients (40), EFD power spectrum (10) + deviation.
3. **Outlier detection** — Mahalanobis distance in PC1–PC2 space; threshold = mean + 3 SD.
4. **Mirror validation** — A/B region pairs compared in morphospace to verify biological signal reproducibility.

### Data

All analysis-ready CSVs are in [`data/`](data/) and can be downloaded directly:

- [`shape_analysis_results.csv`](data/shape_analysis_results.csv) — 1,737 × 82, primary results
- [`shape_summary.csv`](data/shape_summary.csv) — per-class summary (6 × 19)
- [`outliers.csv`](data/outliers.csv) — Mahalanobis distances + outlier flags
- [`mirror_validation.csv`](data/mirror_validation.csv) — 833 A/B pair ranks
- [`hair_morphology_guided.csv`](data/hair_morphology_guided.csv) — basic morphometrics + confidence

### Run locally

```bash
# Install fibermorph with analysis extras
pip install "fibermorph[analysis]"
pip install notebook jupyterlab scipy scikit-learn

# Open notebooks
cd manuscript/analysis
jupyter lab
```
